title: KeyProvider with macOS Keychain
description: Spec §6.4 and §6.1. Evaluate @napi-rs/keyring (backend, pinned version, compiled-binary compatibility) before adopting. A KeyProvider port with a Keychain adapter and a test double. It loads the vault key and creates it only when absent, never replacing an existing key. A locked or unavailable keychain fails within a bounded time. `ward setup` itself moved to WCLI-20 on 2026-09-28, because T01 and T02 need the WCLI-6 store.

acceptanceCriteria.text: KeyProvider loads a vault key and creates one only when none exists, refusing to replace an existing key; a missing, locked, unavailable or wrong-length key yields a fixed catalogue error and never causes a key to be generated (the key side of T02)
The Keychain adapter is exercised through a compiled executable built by scripts/build.ts, and it uses the production service name only outside tests
The keyring binding decision (adopt or reject, with reasons) is recorded in the key-custody ADR

Measured and recorded in docs/adr/0001: whether @napi-rs/keyring stores the item in the legacy file-based keychain or the data-protection keychain, using one throwaway item in a test namespace. The developer authorises that real-keychain write when this task starts; no agent or orchestrator can authorise it
A noninteractive command against a missing, locked or unavailable key fails within a stated bounded time and never waits on a hidden approval prompt

implementationNotes: Criterion 4 measurement, 2026-09-28. My user authorised one throwaway item plus a cross-build read, asked at task start per the orchestrator's ruling. Setup: @napi-rs/keyring 2.1.0 AsyncEntry, bun 1.3.14 --compile with the WCLI-16 flags, macOS arm64, run from this agent's shell. Service opum.ward.probe-034d79b9, a random synthetic 32-byte value that was never printed. Results: (1) BACKEND: setSecret wrote a class genp item into the LEGACY FILE-BASED login keychain (~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db), visible to 'security find-generic-password' with attributes only. It is not the data-protection keychain. (2) SAME-BUILD read (probe-a, cdhash bfdccdf1...): the value came back with no prompt in about 9 ms. (3) CROSS-BUILD read (probe-b, cdhash 8a2b9acd..., different code identity): refused in 16 ms with 'Platform failure: User interaction is not allowed.' (errSecInteractionNotAllowed), and no prompt was shown. This confirms that the ACL trusts the creating build's cdhash only. In this non-GUI agent shell a foreign build fails fast rather than hanging. The GUI-terminal prompt path is NOT measured here. (4) DELETE from the trusting build returned true, and security then reported not found (exit 44); nothing remains. (5) Binding quirks that contradict its own index.d.ts: getSecret resolves a plain number[] rather than a Uint8Array, and null rather than undefined for an absent item. The adapter must normalize both, and a number[] cannot be zeroed reliably. Provenance: MIT licence, SLSA v1 provenance attestations on both @napi-rs/keyring@2.1.0 and @napi-rs/keyring-darwin-arm64@2.1.0.
